answer: A farm running 110 keys therefore burns that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the atlas stake is held until the basalt settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the anchor audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 20% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
